name: BS 1363
description: British 13 A fused plug and shuttered socket-outlet: three rectangular pins in a triangle, the earth pin above line and neutral. Line and neutral pins carry insulating sleeves; the plug holds a BS 1362 cartridge fuse.

variants.name: BS 1363 13 A fused plug
variants.keying: The earth pin enforces polarity. Seen from the pins with the earth pin at the top: line lower left, neutral lower right.
mechanicalNotes: Line and neutral pins 6.4 × 4.0 mm, 17.7 mm long, 22.2 mm between centres, with insulating sleeves.
Earth pin 8.0 × 4.0 mm, 22.2 mm from the line-neutral axis; its length is 22.3 mm on Wikipedia and 22.7 mm on WorldStandards.
Fused with a BS 1362 cartridge fuse in the line path.

variants.name: BS 1363 13 A socket-outlet
variants.keying: Shuttered line and neutral apertures. Seen from the front with the earth aperture at the top: neutral lower left, line lower right.
mechanicalNotes: Apertures at most 7.2 × 4.8 mm (line and neutral) and 8.8 × 4.8 mm (earth).
At least 9.6 mm of insertion before the first live part.
Shutters open with the earth pin on older designs, or with line and neutral (or all three pins) together on others; a two-pin Europlug must not open them.

electricalProfiles.name: AC single-phase
conditions: 13 A comes from the BS 1363 part titles; the 250 V limit comes from a secondary source only.
50 Hz to 60 Hz is in the scope of the 2023 editions.
A plug's marked rating can be lower: it follows the BS 1362 fuse fitted (3 A and 13 A are common). The fuse rating is not the interface rating.

notes: The 250 V limit and all dimensions rely on secondary sources; the BS 1363 texts were not reviewed.
Source conflict on the earth pin length: 22.3 mm (Wikipedia, citing BS 1363-1) against 22.7 mm (WorldStandards). Not stored as a value.
The line and neutral positions of both faces rely on a single secondary source (Wikipedia); the dimensions are confirmed by a second one.
Fused connection units and adaptors (BS 1363-3, -4, -5) are not modelled.
